questions.question:
**Direction: **Fill up the blanks with suitable prepositions.

The way she uses cosmetics is offensive _____ good taste.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'B' i.e. to.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "offensive to good taste" is a common English expression.
 
• Prepositions are used to show the relationships between words in a sentence.
 
• 'To' is often used to indicate a relationship of opposition or impact, which fits the context of the given sentence.

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *The way she uses cosmetics is offensive **to** good taste*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• '**To**' is used to indicate relationships such as direction, destination, or comparison, making it suitable here.

questions.question:
Direction: Fill in the blank in the following sentence with the help of given options.

Today, the need of common man ___________ just bread and butter.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**is**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject '**the need of the common man**' is singular (although it refers to multiple needs, the phrase itself is singular as the "**need**").
 
• So, the **verb **must also be **singular **to maintain subject-verb agreement.
 
• In this case, the singular form of the '**to be**' verb '**is**' is used.
 
• The sentence is in the present tense, as indicated by '**Today**,' reinforcing the use of the present tense '**is**'.

Therefore, the correct answer is ‘**Option 1**’.

 

**Complete Sentence**: *Today, the need of the common man **is**__ just bread and butter.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Option 2: '**are**' is a plural form of the verb 'to be' and does not agree with the singular subject 'the need of the common man'.
 
• Option 3: '**was**' is the past tense of 'is' and does not fit well with the sentence, which is in present tense.
 
• Option 4: '**were**' is also a past tense and plural form of 'is', making it unsuitable for the sentence.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

I have been living in Hyderabad __since I am born__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the present tense** "am" after "since." **The correct** past tense form should be used.**
 
• The correct phrase should be **"since I was born,"** ensuring **grammatical correctness and clarity.**
 
• The use of** "since" **indicates a point in time from the past until now, requiring the past tense "was" to be grammatically correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I have been living in Hyderabad** since I was born."***

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "since I have born,"** – Incorrect because "have born" is not a correct tense form.
 
• **Option 2: "since I will be born,"** – Incorrect because "will be born" indicates future tense, which is not applicable here.
 
• **Option 3: "since I born,"** – Incorrect because "born" without "was" is grammatically incorrect.

questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

Bushfire have created havoc and exacerbated the conditions of animals in the forest.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **error is in **the part: "Bushfire have created havoc"
 
• The **correct form** should be "Bushfires have created havoc".
 
• In English, **subject-verb agreement** is a grammatical rule which states that the subject and verb must agree in number.
 
• That means, if the subject is plural, the verb must be plural.
 
• Conversely, if the **subject is singular, the verb must be singular.**
 
• In this case, **"Bushfire" **is a singular noun, but **"have" **is a plural verb, so they don't agree in number.
 
• The **sentence should be corrected by** changing "Bushfire" to the plural form "Bushfires" to match the plural verb "have".

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'Bushfires have created havoc and exacerbated the conditions of animals in the forest.'*

questions.question:
Fill in the blanks using the correct form of tense -

In the evenings, I often play chess with my next door neighbour. I............ (play) chess with him ever since I..........(come) to live here ten years ago. 1
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**have played; came**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb "**have played**" is in the present perfect tense, indicating an action that began in the past and continues into the present.
 
• The verb "**came**" is in the simple past tense, indicating an action that was completed in the past.
 
• **Options 1, 3**, and **4** are grammatically incorrect in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"In the evenings, I often play chess with my next door neighbour. I **have played**__ chess with him ever since I __**came**__ to live here ten years ago."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "had played; come"** is incorrect because "had played" implies a completed action in the past, and "come" should be in the past tense.
 
• **Option 3: "will play; will came"** is incorrect because "will came" is not a valid future tense construction.
 
• **Option 4: "play; come"** is incorrect because "come" should be in the past tense.

questions.question:

__
 
• The most appropriate option to fill in the blank is **option 3) panic.**
 
• The sentence suggests that a strange noise came from a room, which caused a reaction among the students.
 
• The word **"panic" **fits best in the blank because it describes a sudden feeling of fear or anxiety that can be triggered by an unexpected event or situation.
 
• In this case, the strange noise caused a sense of panic among the students, who were likely frightened or unsure of what was happening.
 
 
• Example: When the fire alarm went off in the building, the employees started to **panic **and rushed towards the exits.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is** Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1) Transport **refers to the act of moving or carrying something from one place to another.

 
 
• For example, a truck might be used to **transport **goods from a factory to a warehouse.
 
 
 
• **Option 2) Deficit** refers to a lack or shortage of something, such as money, resources, or supplies.
 
 
• For example, a government might have a budget **deficit **if its spending exceeds its revenue.
 
 
 
• **Option 4) Civility** refers to politeness and courteous behavior in social situations.
 
 
• For example, a person might be praised for their **civility **if they are polite and respectful towards others.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct option to fill in the blank in the given sentence is **option 3) panic**, as it best describes the reaction of the students to the strange noise coming from the room.

questions.question:

He became increasingly dissatisfied and __querulous__ in his old age.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**cheerful"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Querulous- **If someone is querulous, they are prone to complaining or expressing dissatisfaction in a peevish or petulant manner. (यदि कोई चिड़चिड़े स्वभाव का है, तो वह चिड़चिड़े तरीके से शिकायत करने या असंतोष व्यक्त करने के लिए प्रवृत्त होता है।)

 
 
• **Example: **She became increasingly querulous as the flight was delayed, complaining about everything from the food to the seats
 
 

**Let's see the meanings of the given words**__

__
 
• **Confident-** If someone is confident, they are self-assured and believe in their abilities. (अगर किसी में आत्मविश्वास है तो वे आत्मविश्वासी होते हैं और अपनी क्षमताओं पर विश्वास करते हैं।)

 
 
• **Example:*** She spoke **confidently **in front of a large audience, not showing any signs of nervousness.*
 
 
 
• **Cheerful- **If someone is cheerful, they are happy and upbeat. (यदि कोई हंसमुख है, तो वे खुश और उत्साहित हैं।)
 
 
• **Example:** *Despite the rain, she was in a **cheerful** mood, humming to herself as she worked.*
 
 
 
• **Firm-** If something is firm, it is solid and stable. (यदि कोई चीज दृढ़ है, तो वह ठोस और स्थिर है।)
